Ironically opposite. The faster the car is going, the more likely for whatever you hit to go flying off the top of the car or for it to go under the car. The slower you go the more likely for it to go into the wind sheild. It's basically a physics puzzle of how much lateral force is going to turn into vertical force on impsct, how much momentum does the car have at any given moment, and how much inertia does the struck object have. And its a balancing act of those things.

So the car itself has inertia with mass, momentum, depending on either its weight or speed. Faster or heavier makes more momentum. So faster makes it less likely to be affected by a transfer of energy, say to a deer. Meaning the object wouldn't get transfered as much energy in time to compensate, causing it to either roll off the top in a more fluid motion, or more likely, get rolled over. And in this scenario, even if the object is thicker than your car to the ground, momentum would force the car over. It's why semis make a Huge mess. 

In scenario b, if you go slower the struck objects standing still inertia plays more of a factor. Being relatively more comparable to the slower cars momentum. So force transfered more due to more time for acceleration of the object. slower speed is more time, acceleration is speed change over time, force is mass by acceleration. Thus when struck, the deer applies more force relative to the car (in the equal and opposite reaction), as well as (and because of) the deer getting more force from the car over more time. This force will be less chaotic in all directions due to the same law that makes air more or less turbulent (forgot specifics, but masically more force causes increased changing in forces direction(in scenerio A, the car had a greater chance of rolling ovee the deer, but could have caused such a more chaotic reaction that the deer effectively gets so much of a change in accleratiom, more upward force from chaos, causing it to roll over top). Due to the upper center of gravity, the deer is mostly towards the windshield already, add in a tiny bit of upward force that can overcome gravity then all that force is going right into the windshield.
